takeaway: CD3-engaging bispecific antibodies in haematologic cancers commonly cause cytokine-release syndrome, usually grade 1–2 and within 1–2 days; several blinatumomab studies reported neurologic events in more than half of patients [1].
clinicalQuestion: What efficacy and toxicity pattern do bispecific antibodies show in haematologic neoplasms?
background: Bispecific T-cell engagers bring CD3-positive T cells to a tumour antigen. That mechanism produces a characteristic toxicity [1].
population: Patients with haematologic neoplasms treated with bispecific antibodies.
intervention: Bispecific antibodies, especially CD3 engagers such as blinatumomab, teclistamab, and talquetamab.
primaryOutcome: Response and immune toxicities including cytokine-release syndrome and neurotoxicity.
mainFindings: Cytokine-release syndrome was the most common immune toxicity of CD3-engaging bispecifics. Across studies its incidence ranged from 1.59% to 82.61%. Most events were grade 1–2 and began within 1–2 days. Neurologic events exceeded 50% in several blinatumomab studies. Teclistamab (CD3–BCMA) and talquetamab (CD3–GPRC5D) were associated with frequent cytokine-release syndrome, and neurotoxicity was also reported. Hodgkin and T-cell lymphoma studies were described as early-phase, with limited efficacy and no approvals at the time of the review [1].
clinicalMeaning: Expect early, usually low-grade cytokine release with a CD3 engager, and do not treat a B-cell or myeloma bispecific as if it had the same evidence in Hodgkin lymphoma [1].
limitations: Incidences are ranges across heterogeneous studies, not one drug's label. Approval status is that of the review [1].
bottomLine: Counsel for cytokine-release syndrome in the first day or two, mostly grade 1–2, and for neurotoxicity with CD3 engagers [1].
practiceImplication: Use step-up monitoring because the syndrome starts within 1–2 days, as the review reports [1].
safetyOutcomes: CRS incidence 1.59–82.61%, mostly grade 1–2, onset 1–2 days.
Neurologic events over 50% in several blinatumomab studies.
trustRationale: Systematic review of clinical studies; toxicity ranges are wide because studies were pooled.
whatNotToOverclaim: Do not quote one response rate for every bispecific.
A COVID haematology consensus is not this topic.
